Daily Devotional

November 26

9 Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. (1 John 3:9 KJV)

John is not saying that a Christian cannot sin, as in the same letter he says that if we say we do not sin, then we are liars (1 John 1:8). What he is saying is that when we do sin, it does not affect our born again spirits, as our spirits are of God, and cannot sin. When we are born again our new spirits, that were created holy and righteous (Ephesians 4:24), are sealed (Ephesians 1:13), and even if we sin, it does not penetrate our new spirits, which remain holy and righteous, because it was born of God. Even though a born again Christian is living in the spirit, he can still walk after the flesh and sin. This means a Christian’s spirit is now righteous in the sight of God, but his body is still able to live after the flesh and commit sin. A person, who was truly born again, should always have the desire to live holy, as God is holy (1 Peter 1:16), and changes your heart to desire to be like him.

Some have thought that we can eventually become righteous in all our actions, and never sin, but that is not what the bible teaches. As long as we are living in these bodies, we will sin, as this world and the devil will see to it. We can never claim to be holy enough on our own, to be right with God, but we will always need to put our faith in what Jesus has done for us. We will always need a Savior to save us from hell, and bring us into fellowship with the Father and Jesus (John 17:3) (which is what everlasting life means). Don’t fall back into the works of the law, thinking that you can be holy enough to be saved, as if we don’t put all our trust for salvation on Jesus, then we are denying the Cross, and making Jesus of no effect in our lives (Galatians 5:4). If you are truly born again, you desire to live a holy life for God, but not condemned if you do sin. A Christian should have no more conscience of sin (Romans 8:1), but religion still tries to teach us to be thinking about sin all the time. All our thoughts need to be on Jesus, and what He did, not on what we do. Thank you Lord for our wonderful salvation!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Even people with actual genetic disorders have more self-control than fat "people"...

Short version:

Abby Solomon suffers from a one-in-a-billion genetic syndrome: After just about an hour without food, she begins to starve. She sleeps in snatches. In her dreams she gorges on French fries. But as soon as she wakes up and nibbles a few bites, she feels full, so she ends up consuming very few calories. At 5 feet 10 inches tall, she weighs 99 pounds.

Now 21 years old, she is one of the few people in the world to survive into adulthood with neonatal progeroid syndrome, a condition that results from damage to the FBN1 gene. This mutation mangles noses and eyes and destroys the layer of fat under the skin so that even teenagers look middle-aged. It also interferes with the body’s ability to make a hormone called asprosin, which regulates blood sugar. Atul Chopra, a medical geneticist at Baylor College of Medicine, told me that people with the disorder don’t experience ordinary hunger — instead they waver on the edge of hypoglycemia and must constantly snack to keep from passing out.

[...]

“Nothing comes close to starting with people who are naturally different,” he said. This is why he searches out patients at the extreme ends of the spectrum — those who are wired to weigh 80 pounds or 380 pounds. He said, “We have the opportunity to help a bigger swath of humanity when we learn from these outliers.”

And from further on in the article, in an anecdote about a restaurant visit:
